commits.message: fix(url-handle): a busy click exits 0, and frames-cli takes its kick from the render policy (candybar-launch-q7o7.4yv)
fix(client): busy is its own outcome kind, and a click waits past the daemon's backstop (candybar-launch-q7o7.4yv)

fix(url-handle): a daemon's TIMEOUT is busy, and a click's client no longer kicks a live daemon (candybar-launch-q7o7.4yv)

Replaces the raised click bound: the daemon answering TIMEOUT proves it is
up, so the client tells it from a wait it gave up and only kicks when no
daemon answered. The 200ms bound, the applet's quick return and the
journal's stale-click refusal stay as they were.

fix(daemon): a click is held to a click's bound, so a launching click no longer kicks a live daemon (candybar-launch-q7o7.4yv)

The connection backstop answered every request TIMEOUT at the render's
200ms. A click awaits the program it launches (up to 5s), so the client
heard TIMEOUT, kicked a daemon that was up, and exited 1 while the
click's effect still landed. The backstop is now re-armed by request
kind once the frame is read, and the click client's budget derives from
the daemon's click bound.
fix(frame-feed): setTimer clears the timer it replaces, so no caller can orphan one (brandon-unfiled-3248.l1mh)
fix(frame-feed): review of the early-fire wait: reflow the bound's comment, correct the memory line, test a second early fire and a close while waiting (brandon-unfiled-3248.l1mh)

fix(frame-feed): a timer that fires before its moment waits it out, so no turn is drawn twice (brandon-unfiled-3248.l1mh)

Node starts a timer from the loop's cached time, so one armed late in a slow
callback fires early by as long as that callback had run. Past
TIMER_RESOLUTION_S the draw clamped to the wall, which fell in the turn before
the frame's change: that turn drawn twice, the next one late. The feed now
compares the timer's moment on the monotonic clock and re-arms for the rest.

test(ci): every CI run stores one record per test file (candybar-testing-ihvy.myy) (#564)

* test(ci): every CI run stores one record per test file (candybar-testing-ihvy.myy)

A reporter writes test-records/<run>.jsonl, one record per file: layer, count,
duration, outcome and each case. A file jest never gave a result for reads
never-ran and a file with no test reads empty, so neither passes for the other
or for absent. test:report prints count and time per layer and the jest wall
time from those records, and fails for a run that left none. CI uploads the
records.

* test(ci): the records reporter reads lost files off the run, so -o and --shard record (candybar-testing-ihvy.myy)

Jest counts the files it scheduled after every narrowing, so the reporter takes
the lost-file count from the run and asks the search to name files only when
that count is above zero. Asked every run, the search threw under -o and read
every file of a shard as lost. The test report and upload now follow the
protocol and Rust gates, and the wall-time label says it spans the test files.

* test(ci): the colour audits write their own run's records (candybar-testing-ihvy.myy)

The audits config spreads the suite's, so it inherited the "all" run and wrote
over a local full-suite record.

docs(design): the isolated daemon, tmux events and browser surface designs

Goals, architecture, contracts and one document per area, with the surveys and probes behind them. The Frame is recorded as built, and the browser surface is un-parked.
fix(bar-pane): a frame overwrites its rows and lands whole, so the pane stops flickering
